Write SCENE LS1 (1 of 5) of a natural Mandarin LISTENING conversation between two people for a learner.
WHOLE CONVERSATION: two friends meet, catch up and talk about everyday things (shopping & payment, home, feelings)
SPEAKERS: A = Speaker A (friend) · B = Speaker B (friend) · A and B are friends talking; natural, casual-polite spoken Mandarin (simplified characters).
REGISTER: natural spoken · friendly
THIS SCENE: A and B meet and start talking about today
ONE CONVERSATION — the learner hears ONE continuous conversation; this request writes its next PART (part 1, internal only — never announce it).
CONVERSATION CONTRACT: speakers A = Speaker A (friend) · B = Speaker B (friend) · relationship: friends · opening location: where they meet · objective: spend time together: meet → decide where to go → go there → do / eat / buy → pay · ending goal: they finish what they set out to do and say goodbye
STORY SO FAR: (nothing yet — this part opens the conversation)
NEXT PART GOAL: see THIS SCENE above.
- Do NOT say goodbye: the conversation continues afterwards. End this part on an answer or a statement, not on an open question.
LATER PARTS will use: 开, 觉得, 说, 拿, 工作, 人, 一起, 到, 真的, 听, 帮, 找, 太, 家, 知道, 回, 用, 做, 买, 钱, 看, 地方, 东西 (leave them for later).
SCENE INTENT: WHO the same two friends throughout · WHERE where they meet · SITUATION A and B meet and start talking about today · WHY they talk: spend time together: meet → decide where to go → go there → do / eat / buy → pay · WHAT they want to achieve: A and B meet and start talking about today. Every turn moves this goal on; a target that does not fit the goal is used in a short natural aside, never a random topic jump.
CONTEXT SO FAR: this is the opening scene — start with a natural greeting
SCENE SHAPE: the exchanges pursue the scene goal; the scene ENDS with that goal resolved (they decide, agree, pay, or say goodbye). Lesson words are heard inside real talk — never a list of sentences about each word.
CLOSED WORLD — PRIORITY ORDER: 1. use ONLY the vocabulary listed here · 2. use every required target · 3. correct grammar · 4. the learner level · 5. be natural WITHIN those limits. Naturalness never justifies a word that is not listed.

  T2 B ANSWER — B answers with yes / no (or a qualified answer) ⟨must give yes / no (or a qualified answer)⟩ · no lesson word required · SUPPORT: 怎么样 可以 怎么 很 这个 我 · PROVEN: 懂。
  T3 A QUESTION(what) — A asks B what (using 等 "wait") · REQUIRED: 等 "wait" · SUPPORT: 怎么样 这个 那个 没关系 没事 可以 · PROVEN: 你等什么？
  T4 B ANSWER — B answers with the thing asked about (using 朋友 "friend") ⟨must give the thing asked about⟩ · REQUIRED: 朋友 "friend" · SUPPORT: 怎么样 这个 那个 没关系 没事 可以 · PROVEN: 我等朋友。
  T5 A QUESTION(how it is) — A asks B how it is · no lesson word required · SUPPORT: 这个 好 那个 怎么样 可以 怎么 · PROVEN: 这个怎么样？

  T8 B ANSWER — B answers with yes / no (or a qualified answer) (using 多 "many") ⟨must give yes / no (or a qualified answer)⟩ · REQUIRED: 多 "many" · SUPPORT: 怎么样 可以 怎么 很 这个 我 · PROVEN: 很多。

ROLE GUIDE: CONTENT = the topic of a turn · DESCRIPTION = a reaction or comment on something · ACTION = what someone does or will do
LENGTH: 8–8 turns. HARD MAXIMUM 8 turns.
EACH TURN: CURRENT LEVEL: Shodan · PREFERRED LENGTH: 4–16 Mandarin words · ABSOLUTE MAXIMUM: 20 Mandarin words (polite / question / sentence-final particles do not count). Prefer 4–16 — the shortest natural way to say it. Use 17–20 only when the idea or the lesson word cannot be said naturally more simply. Never exceed 20. A short natural reply ("yes", "okay", "really?") is fine — never pad a line. If a speaker needs to say more, split it into another turn. Keep the situation simple enough to say at this level — one idea per turn (e.g. "How much is it?" / "Ten thousand baht." / "That is expensive."), never explanations in one long turn.
RULES:
- Each turn is ONE speaker; questions get answers; never put a question and its answer in the same turn; A and B both speak.
- At most 3 lesson words per turn (the required words above AND these other lesson words count: 钱, 买, 人, 东西, 地方, 家, 工作, 真的, 觉得, 知道, 说, 听, 看, 帮, 找, 做, 用, 拿, 开, 回, 到, 一起, 太).
- Response words (yes / no / yeah …) are used as REPLIES. No repeated sentences. No filler turns that do nothing.
- Do not say goodbye yet; the conversation continues in the next scene.
- Content words ONLY from the required targets and the ALLOWED SUPPORT VOCABULARY above. No personal names. Give tone-mark "pinyin" for every turn.
